name: Null’s Apps
subtitle: NullSign and Lineup for iPhone and Apple TV
description: Unsigned iOS and tvOS app builds published after successful main-branch builds.

apps.name: NullSign
apps.subtitle: Sign and install iOS apps
apps.localizedDescription: NullSign signs and installs iOS apps right on your iPhone with your own certificate. Import IPAs from Files or a URL, browse AltStore-compatible sources, and install in one tap. It keeps your apps up to date, updates itself, and installs Apple TV apps on your paired Apple TV over Wi-Fi.

versions.localizedDescription:
• This was supposed to go out with the smaller fixes from ten minutes ago. Oops. Enjoy the double update.
• Added Update All in Sources updates with search, per-app source picking, and a choice to just add, sign, or sign and install—because tapping Update twelve times in a row was getting old.
• Long-pressing grouped updates actually has options now, including Ignore Updates for that one app you refuse to update.
• Automatic Cleanup can now wipe same or newer copies too, not just older ones, if you like keeping your Library spotless.
• Updates now keep your existing copy's bundle ID so they actually replace it instead of cloning a second copy onto your Home Screen, and the Identifier editor lists the ones already in your Library.
• Big apps shouldn't panic and yell Failed while iOS is still unpacking them, installs shouldn't stall halfway, tiny apps shouldn't claim they failed right after succeeding, reused update rows show the right icon now, and View in Sources won't drop you into a black void.

• Pulling to refresh inside a repo no longer leaves the search bar chilling in the middle of the screen blocking your apps. Turns out people actually wanted to see those.
• Pulling down on the Apps screen now lets you know it's updating instead of flashing the spinner for half a second and gaslighting you into thinking nothing happened.

• NullSign no longer freezes halfway through updating itself and just stares at you. Tap Install and it gets out of the way so iOS can do its thing.
• The full-screen update page is back, so new builds are harder to miss. Yes, that's how you're reading this.
• Skipped a few updates? The update pop-up now shows what's new in every build you missed, not just the latest one.

• Apple TV installs are a lot faster now, and they don't get stuck on "Installing" anymore. No more opening and closing the app on your TV to get it going.
• If an Apple TV install ever does stall, NullSign tells you how to get it moving instead of just sitting there.

• Apple TV installs connect more reliably, and if the first try doesn't go through, NullSign quietly tries again for you.
• When NullSign updates itself, it waits until the update has fully arrived before stepping aside, so the new version finishes much faster.
• Signed apps keep their provisioning profile, so they install on devices that haven't seen them before, like a brand new Apple TV. Signed an Apple TV app on an earlier 2.0 build? Sign it again.

• Your library stops offering updates for NullSign's own copies.
• If an Apple TV turns down an app's profile, NullSign tells you why. You can also copy your Apple TV's UDID from its spot in Settings for your certificate provider.
• When you install a NullSign update, NullSign now steps out of the way so the new version can finish installing on its own.

• NullSign spots its own updates within half an hour, and one tap in About or on the Signer card installs it.
• Tap Update and NullSign downloads, signs and installs the new version right over your app again. Check for Updates finishes quickly too.
• Pull down on Sources and every source fetches a fresh copy. If one can't, its card tells you.

• Updates stick with the tweaked build you downloaded, so X or Instagram won't jump to a different tweak. If NullSign can't tell which one you want, it asks.
• IPAs you open from other apps now say Open in NullSign.
• Signed apps carry their provisioning profile again, so they install on devices that haven't seen it before.
• Coming from 1.5.2 with an Apple TV set up? Installs work again instead of saying Missing Pairing, and iPhone apps sign with your iPhone certificate.
• NullSign goes by its own name everywhere you see it now, and backups save as a .nullsignbackup file.

• Pick a few apps at once and sign, install or delete them together. You can also drag apps around to put your library in your own order.
• Installs line up now. Start a few and they go one after another. Close the card and a small pill keeps track, and you can cancel the one that's running.
• When an app is in more than one source, you choose where its update comes from, and NullSign can remember that. Skip an update you don't want and it stops asking.
• Star your favorite sources to keep them on top, hide a source from All Apps without deleting it, and sort your sources however you like.
• Sources open from a saved copy first, so the Apps tab fills in right away, even on a slow connection.
• Back up your certificates, sources, settings and tweaks to one file, then restore them on another device or after a reset.
• Web Manager lets you move IPAs and files between NullSign and a computer from any browser on the same Wi-Fi.
• Storage shows what's taking up space and lets you clear it out. Activity Logs keep a record if something goes wrong.
• Tweaks get their own library, and you choose which ones go into every app you sign.
• Edit an app's Info.plist and entitlements right from the signing screen before you sign.
• Apple TV has its own spot in Settings. Apple TV apps pick your tvOS certificate on their own, and certificates that work for Apple TV get a tvOS tag.
• Null's Apps comes built in, so NullSign and Lineup are there from the first launch.

• Full screen on iPhone Duo. The tab bar sits on the right like the rest of the phone, next to your toolbar buttons when it's tucked away.
• Switched to the regular iOS tab bar. Tap the tab you're already on to jump back to its first screen. The Signer badge still counts your waiting updates.
• Installs finish on Completed with a checkmark, even when iOS stops reporting progress right at the end.
• Deleting an app from your library happens right away, and you'll know if it didn't save. Imported apps show their real icons.
• If an IPA from Files won't import, you'll see why instead of it just disappearing.
• PPQ protection is gone. Apps are signed with their own bundle ID.
• A source with a missing file tells you that, instead of a confusing invalid JSON error. GitHub sources can drop out for a minute while a new release uploads.

• Fixed a crash when installing imported apps with ElleKit enabled.
• ElleKit is now enabled by default for new or reset signing settings. Your saved preference is kept.
• Invalid or incomplete .deb tweaks now show an error instead of closing NullSign.

• Tap Install on an imported app to sign it with your saved certificate and settings, then continue straight to installation.
• The same progress bar now follows preparation, signing, packaging and installation. Errors stay in the progress card with a Retry action.
• The usual iPhone install flow skips the browser's extra Open prompt while keeping iOS's Install confirmation. Continue in Browser is available if needed.
• Repository icons now update from the latest source feed when you refresh, including the icons beside All Apps.

• Fixed installs hanging in Safari and ending with "the server stopped responding" on some cellular carriers. NullSign now installs from your Wi-Fi address, never your cellular one.
• Without Wi-Fi, installs go through the phone itself, the same as the Use localhost only setting.

• New setting: Keep Only the Newest Version, in Settings › Signing Defaults › Library. When a newer version of an app arrives, older copies of it are deleted from Imported and from Signed.
• Turning it on clears out duplicate and older copies already in your library. Apps installed on your device stay installed.
• An older version you import on purpose is kept, and an app being signed or updated never loses the copy it just made.

• Update on a signed app now updates it in one tap. NullSign downloads the new version, signs it with the same certificate, then asks iOS to install it over the old one.
• While an app updates, its row shows Downloading update and Signing update, and if something goes wrong NullSign tells you why.
• Fixed tapping Update on a signed app reinstalling the version you already had.

apps.name: Lineup
apps.subtitle: Live TV, sports, and your media library
apps.localizedDescription: Lineup puts your IPTV provider and your media servers in one app. Watch live channels with a full TV guide, catch up on what you missed, or put two channels side by side. Find any game in Sports and jump straight to the channel showing it. Browse movies and shows from Jellyfin, Emby, Plex or Silo, pick up where you left off, and request what's missing through Seerr.

versions.localizedDescription:
• Gave the whole iPhone app a proper redesign because half the tabs looked like stuff I threw together at 2am and forgot to go back to. Everything actually matches now.
• Sports got a clean new header, a Featured Live card at the top, OT and CLOSE tags for tight games, better score contrast so you can actually tell who's winning, followed team stars, collapsible Final scores, and a way nicer All Sports menu.
• TV Guide now has quick shortcuts at the top, real category icons with channel counts, a cleaner timeline with a proper Now line, and Up Next in the mini player. Also finally killed that huge annoying Refreshing Data popup and swapped it for a small pill instead.
• Fixed five different poster bugs that were leaving half your Library as blank gray boxes. Timed out requests actually retry now instead of staying broken forever, slow servers won't hang the loader, and missing server or episode art falls back to TMDB. Also put real Silo, Emby, and Jellyfin logos in the Library switcher.
• Search now shows result counts on the filter tabs plus Recent Searches, and Genre Browse stopped listing the exact same movie twice like it has amnesia.
• Cleaned up Settings with side-by-side Live TV and Media Servers status cards and a better Apple TV pairing screen so you can actually see what's connected without tapping through three menus.

• Skip Intro actually skips the intro now instead of sitting there looking pretty while I stare at the theme song again.
• I rebuilt the playback options menu from scratch because the old one looked like it came free with a 2012 cable box. Stats, Video, Audio, Subtitles, and Chapters finally look like they belong in the same app.
• Fullscreen controls react when you tap them now instead of making you double-check whether your thumb stopped working.
• Updated AetherEngine to 7.71.2 under the hood so streams open faster and stop throwing tantrums mid-play.

• Live TV gets a moment to catch its breath while data is still coming in. We’ve retired the panic button that kept restarting the stream.
• If a live stream URL gives up, Lineup tries another one from your provider before firing the entire playback engine.
• A movie that disconnects halfway through stays in Continue Watching. Nice try, credits.
• Silo search results now look up the playable files. A very good place to look for something to play.

• Tap a game that hasn't started to open its own page: the league's logo, when and where it's on, how each team has been doing lately, a reminder button, and Where to Watch.
• Where to Watch lists the channels your guide confirms from every playlist you've added, then that network's own channels, like ESPN, from each one.
• Hold a live game and pick Channels to get that same list, and any channel in it plays.
• The Library's dropdown now switches between Lineup's Library and each server's own. Everything that menu used to hold is in Settings, under Library.
• Playing something from a server's Library only looks for streams on that server.
• 4K HDR and Dolby Vision movies from Silo play directly instead of asking your server to convert them.

• Pick Media Server Libraries in the Library menu to browse a single server the way its own app lays it out: its recommended rows, the whole library with sorting, filters and Shuffle, and its collections.
• Silo posters show the same quality badges as Silo's own app, like 1080P, EAC3 and REMUX.
• Up Next has its own row now, apart from Continue Watching.
• Movies and shows from every IPTV account you've added show up in the VOD row, and the Library menu lets you see all of them or just one. Tap a folder to browse its categories and open any title.
• The stream list puts each provider's VOD first, named after the account, then your servers, then add-on results, and file sizes are back on every stream.
• Each provider's tab in the stream list counts only its own streams and stops spinning once it's done looking.
• Silo streams play instead of getting stuck on Reconnecting.
• Starting a movie or show stops any live channel that was still playing.
• Plex isn't supported anymore. If you had a Plex server saved, it's skipped and your other servers load as usual.

• Everything feels quicker: the TV Guide scrolls sideways without stutter, and Sports and the Library don't redraw things that haven't changed.
• College basketball games get their channel in Sports whenever the TV Guide shows them on one, small-school games on ESPN+ included.
• Top 25 numbers only show up next to teams that are actually ranked.
• Library shelf titles are just text now, without the icons.
• After a reinstall, Trending Movies, Trending Shows and Streaming Services fill in on their own instead of leaving the Library empty.

• Setting up an Apple TV from your phone brings everything over in one go now, so there's no reopening the app until it all shows up. If the first try can't reach the TV, it tries again on its own.
• College basketball is here: every Division I game, the latest AP or Coaches Top 25 next to teams, live stats, and all 365 teams to follow in My Teams. The ranking setting is called College Top 25 now and covers football too.
• UFC cards show every channel carrying them, not just one.
• On an unfolded iPhone Duo, expanding a game in Sports puts the picture on the top half and keeps the scores, stats or games on the bottom half. Fold it into laptop mode and the picture sits on the top screen.
• Live stats scroll as one page under the picture, instead of in a small box at the bottom.

• Got two IPTV providers? Each one has its own section in the TV Guide now, with its own favorites, recently watched and all channels. Tap a provider's name to open or close it. Categories go by their own names, without the provider in front.
• The TV Guide opens right on your categories with no bar on top. You no longer get stuck inside a default category or Favorites, every row opens when you tap it, and list view stops hiding the first channel.
• Lock the screen while you watch. Tap the lock in the player and touches, swipes and turning the phone are ignored. Hold the lock to unlock.
• Turn off sports you don't watch, from the Sports tab's league list or Settings. College football rankings stay current, and you can pick AP, Coaches or Playoff in Settings.
• The live score bar rolls smoothly from game to game, and the extra clock at the top is gone since your phone already shows the time.
• On an unfolded iPhone Duo, Sports and the TV Guide put their headers up next to the clock. The TV Guide's video preview is bigger, without the large channel name over it.
• The Library scrolls smoothly again. Posters fit the screen, the artwork fades to black under the ratings, shelves run edge to edge, and landscape collections fill their tiles.

• The TV Guide opens on your channel categories now, like other IPTV apps: Favorites, Recently Watched, All Channels, then your provider's categories. Tap one to see its guide. Hold a category to open the guide on it every time, or to hide it.
• On iPhone Duo the tabs sit on the side, and the Library artwork, shelves and TV Guide header go all the way to the edge of the screen.
• Library shelves are Liquid Glass on iOS 26.
• Search has a type menu, so you can look at just movies, shows, VOD or your collections. Collections can be filtered to movies or TV shows too.
• The stream list, channel pickers, Catch Up and team pages open full screen. From the Start on a show starts the episode over like it should.
• Seerr lets you request single seasons and tells you why something can't be requested. Silo takes the address from its docs page when you set it up, and stops playback properly when you're done.

• The smaller iPhone download includes AetherEngine 7.62.1 and MPVKit. MPVKit can take over when AetherEngine can’t open a stream.
• The Library hero uses backdrop artwork. Pick multiple catalogs for the hero or shuffle titles across your catalogs.
• You can hide the built-in genre categories in Search and move stream badges above the server’s formatted text.
• Switching My Teams or changing leagues now starts the schedule at the top, with live games and upcoming days in separate rows.

• Continue Watching shows the series name and poster, with one thin bar along the bottom for the episode or movie you paused.
• Switch Jellyfin profiles from the Library and see each person's profile picture. You can also sign in with Quick Connect.
• On AIO Jellyfin servers, Continue Watching follows the selected profile's resume list.
• The TV Guide keeps the last channel in view when you scroll to the bottom or change categories.
• Look for Lineup's new three-bar icon on your Home Screen.

• Shows you're caught up on stay in Continue Watching, with the next episode's air date, or a Coming Soon card until one is scheduled.
• With two servers connected, like Nullfin and AIOStreams, a movie or show shows up once in Continue Watching, and your progress reaches both servers whichever one played it.
• Continue Watching keeps up with your other devices: something you finish on the Apple TV moves on here too, and Lineup checks again whenever you come back to the app.
• Nullfin and other Jellyfin servers' streams now show exactly the way your formatter writes them, like AIOStreams' do.
• Games that won't load move to another channel within about 15 seconds instead of minutes, and Lineup remembers channels that failed and tries the working ones first next time.
• Ambient Mode spreads the picture's colours into the black bars around it, like YouTube. Turn it off in Metadata settings.
• Show names in the TV Guide no longer carry the tiny raised "New" some providers add; new episodes get a clean NEW badge instead.

• The player has a new look built on Liquid Glass on iOS 26: close at the top left, picture in picture at the top right, bigger play and skip buttons in the middle, and the title right on the picture instead of in a box.
• Subtitles, audio, the next episode and the summary are together in one toolbar at the bottom right, and the progress bar is a thin line along the bottom.
• Full screen in Sports and the TV Guide, the player has the same look, with live stats and other channels for the game in the toolbar at the bottom right.

• Your progress now syncs with Jellyfin, Emby and AIOStreams. The server knows where you stopped, and what you watch in other apps shows up in Continue Watching and Next Up. You can turn it off with Server Tracking in your tracking settings.
• AIOStreams streams are listed exactly the way your formatter writes them. Turn off Server's Stream Format in Metadata settings to go back to Lineup's own layout.
• Add badge packs by link under Stream Badges, and streams get picture badges for things like 4K, Dolby Vision or Atmos. Packs made for the AIOStreams app, Fusion or Nuvio work as they are.
• AIOStreams streams come up faster: Lineup starts finding them as soon as you open a movie or episode.
• Posters from your own server, such as ones from a poster service, now stay put instead of being swapped for TMDB's. Server Posters in Metadata settings turns this off.
• Collection, folder and streaming service cards no longer leave empty space under their names.
• The player's buttons and panels use Liquid Glass on iOS 26.
• Late games that run past midnight stay on the Sports list until they end, wherever you are.

• Finishing the newest episode of a show that's still airing keeps your place. It no longer jumps to the specials or back to the first episode, and the next episode shows up in Continue Watching once it's announced.
• Episode cards show the air date and running time right under the episode's name.
• Adding an AIOStreams server sets up your Library straight away: its libraries appear as shelves in the order you arranged them, and the banner at the top fills itself.
• AIOStreams collections show their full wide artwork instead of being cropped, and the banner at the top of Library only features movies and shows, never collection art.
• You can now remove the Collections row from the Library's Remove Shelf menu, and bring it back from Add Shelf.
• Library lists no longer say "0 titles" for libraries whose size the server doesn't report.

• The posters in Library's Streaming Services row now come to life. Each one shows art from that service's most popular titles you can play, drifting slowly and fading to the next title every few seconds.
• The posters stay smooth while you scroll and take turns changing, so the row never changes all at once. With Reduce Motion on, each poster shows a still picture instead.
• With an AIOStreams server added, Library opens faster and stays lighter: Lineup no longer loads every one of your catalogs each time you open the app. Your collections still show in the Collections row, and a collection's titles load when you open it.
• When there's no featured banner at the top of Library, the first row no longer sits under the clock.

• Reduced slowdowns when opening live events, switching tabs and browsing large libraries while channels and guide data refresh in the background.
• Settings scrolls smoothly as the navigation bar compacts and reappears.
• Live scores refresh independently of channel matching, and tennis events keep their prepared channels when tournament listings change.
• Fixed an earlier stream starting after you had already stopped playback or selected another stream.
• Added soccer coverage for the Carabao Cup, FA Cup, Copa del Rey and Supercopa de España.
• Device Reports in Diagnostics can now copy saved reports with the installed build and iOS version.
• This iPhone release has no user-facing changes.

• Returning to Lineup shows saved live events and their matched channels sooner, so you can open a game while schedules and TV listings refresh in the background.
• Saved alternative channels are ready alongside the main feed, including when the original channel's listing has ended.
• The data refresh popup now appears only in TV Guide.
• The glass navigation bar compacts and expands with a smoother transition, respecting Reduce Motion.

apps.name: Lineup tvOS
apps.subtitle: Live television, sports, and your media library on Apple TV
apps.localizedDescription: Lineup brings your IPTV provider and your media servers to Apple TV. Browse live channels in the TV guide, open a game in Sports right on the channel showing it, and watch movies and shows from Jellyfin, Emby, Plex or Silo, picking up where you left off. Request what's missing through Seerr.

versions.localizedDescription:
• If live TV and sports felt laggy no matter which player you picked, yeah that was on me. The app was basically fighting itself in the background. I paused background IPTV catalog and EPG refreshes during fullscreen and multiview, stopped Ambient Glow from taking live video screenshots every 2.5 seconds, cut out a bunch of main-thread clock and display-link spam, fixed the tvOS audio session, and gave VLC, Aether, and MPV real live buffers (4s VLC cache, 64 MiB MPV cache with auto-reconnect, and stopped forcing fast-zap on Aether for Apple TV).
• Redesigned the whole Apple TV app to match the new iPhone look. New top bar, smaller refresh toast, cleaner Sports cards with OT and CLOSE tags, better score contrast, channel pills, collapsible Final Scores, and real league logos in the All Sports picker.
• Added Manage Categories to the TV Guide with search, Show All / Hide All, and quick one-click Select toggles that sync with iPhone, so hiding 30 IPTV categories you'll never touch doesn't take all afternoon.
• TV Guide got quick-access cards, real category icons, NEW and UHD badges, and Up Next previews. Settings also got the new side-by-side Live TV and Media Servers status cards with real Silo, Emby, and Jellyfin logos.
• Rewrote how tvOS loads Library posters so you stop getting random gray boxes, added TMDB fallback art and green watched badges, brought Recent Searches to Apple TV, and fixed Genre Browse showing duplicate titles.
• Pressing Up from Sports or Library actually gets you back to the top nav bar now instead of trapping you there until you give up and hit Back.

• Skip Intro finally obeys the remote instead of acting like a decorative coaster. Hit Select and it actually jumps.
• I redesigned the playback options menu because the old one looked painfully cheap. Info, Stats, Video, Audio, Subtitles, and Chapters now look like I actually cared—because I did.
• Fullscreen controls feel snappy without playing leapfrog over half the buttons when you click across the bar.
• Updated AetherEngine to 7.71.2 and taught Lineup to remember whichever live stream transport actually works for your provider—so channels start fast instead of flashing Reconnecting and drifting out of sync.
• Scrolling down from the Settings tab lands in the main settings sidebar now, and backing out of a sub-setting puts you right back on the category you picked instead of teleporting you to Library.

• Lineup stops restarting live streams that are still buffering. Turns out throwing away the buffer doesn’t make buffering faster.
• An early disconnect no longer marks a movie watched. You still get to find out who did it.
• The TV Guide keeps the current category on screen until the next one is ready. Farewell, spontaneous black rectangle.
• Press Up from the first playback option to return to your tab. No more surprise field trips to Chapters.
• Silo search results now look up the playable files. The play button has been briefed.

• 4K HDR and Dolby Vision movies from Silo play directly instead of asking your server to convert them.
• Playing something from a server's Library only looks for streams on that server.
• Moving up to the tabs lands on the tab you're already on instead of jumping to Library.
• Scrolling the TV Guide no longer jumps back a few channels.
• The TV Guide's text is bigger and easier to read.

• The tabs along the top and anything you highlight now lift up with a soft shadow, with no white box or frame around them.
• Pick a server from the row at the top of the Library to browse it the way its own app lays it out: its recommended rows, the whole library with sorting and filters, and its collections.
• Sports, the TV Guide and the Library respond faster and stay smooth while you move around.
• Hold Select on a TV Guide category to hide it, and bring it back from Hidden Categories at the bottom of the list.
• Trending movies and shows show up in Lineup's spot on the Home Screen's Top Shelf.
• Player controls are much easier to see when highlighted, and pressing Up from the seek bar takes you to Next Episode.
• Up Next has its own row in the Library, apart from Continue Watching.
• Silo streams play instead of getting stuck on Reconnecting, and the stream list shows VOD first with file sizes back.
• Plex isn't supported anymore. If you had a Plex server saved, it's skipped and your other servers load as usual.

• If the TV Guide shows a college basketball game on a channel, Sports finds that channel too, including small-school games on ESPN+.
• Only teams that are actually in the Top 25 get a number beside them.
• The Trending and Streaming Services rows no longer stay missing for the rest of the day when they're first built before your servers have loaded.

• Set Up with iPhone looks like the rest of the app and stays up until your channels and library have loaded, then says you're all set. Everything comes over in one go.
• The TV Guide opens on your categories, like on iPhone: Favorites, Recently Watched, All Channels, then the rest. Moving across the tab bar no longer drops you into it.
• College basketball is here, with the latest Top 25 and every Division I team to follow. Choose which sports show up, and which Top 25 you see, in Settings under Sports.
• Choose a Channel lists every channel carrying a game, so a UFC card shows all of its channels.
• If the app ever closes on its own, the Playback Log says so next time, along with what was playing.

• The TV Guide's channel menu starts with Favorites, Recently Watched and All Channels, then your categories. Recently Watched is new here.
• Turn off sports you don't watch in Settings, under Sports. They drop out of the Sports tab and its sport filter.
• Pick which college football ranking shows next to teams: AP, which is the default, Coaches or Playoff. Rankings stay current.

• Seerr requests go season by season, and you'll see why a title or season can't be requested instead of a generic error.
• Setting up Silo works with the address from its docs page, and playback sessions end properly when you stop watching.
• If the sports schedule can't refresh because of a secure connection problem, it tells you that.

• Immersive lighting stays inside the black bars during playback. The light bands are half as deep.
• Scrolling through Library posters does less work, and moving focus stops animated artwork from decoding after you leave a card.
• Coming back from the screensaver is smoother, especially with a large watch history or a connected Jellyfin server.
• Stream results show the release’s file size when the server provides it, including when you use your server’s formatter.

• Shows you're caught up on stay in Continue Watching, with the next episode's air date, or a Coming Soon card until one is scheduled.
• With two servers connected, like Nullfin and AIOStreams, a movie or show shows up once in Continue Watching, and your progress reaches both servers whichever one played it.
• Continue Watching keeps up with your iPhone: something you finish there moves on here too.
• Nullfin and other Jellyfin servers' streams now show exactly the way your formatter writes them, like AIOStreams' do.
• Games that won't load move to another channel within about 15 seconds instead of minutes, and Lineup remembers channels that failed and tries the working ones first next time.
• Ambient Mode spreads the picture's colours into any black bars around it. Turn it off in Metadata settings.
• Search lists its genres from A to Z, and show names in the guide no longer carry the tiny raised "New" some providers add.

• Your progress now syncs with Jellyfin, Emby and AIOStreams. The server knows where you stopped, and what you watch in other apps shows up in Continue Watching and Next Up.
• Animated covers play on the card you're on and stop when you move away.
• AIOStreams streams are listed exactly the way your formatter writes them, and badge packs you add in Metadata settings put picture badges under each stream.
• AIOStreams streams come up faster: Lineup starts finding them as soon as you open a movie or episode.
• Posters from your own server, such as ones from a poster service, now stay put instead of being swapped for TMDB's.
• Late games that run past midnight stay on Sports until they end, wherever you are.

• Lineup on Apple TV is simpler and much faster. Sports is now a list of game cards like on iPhone: select a game to watch it full screen, or hold select for channels, reminders, team pages and more.
• In the TV Guide, Back takes you to the top of the guide, and Back again to the menu bar. Browsing channels no longer starts a video for each one; select a channel to watch it.
• Library shows all your shelves in one scrolling list.
• Scrolling is smoother on every tab. If the screen ever freezes for a moment, Settings › Screen Stalls shows when and what was happening.
• Finishing the newest episode of a show that's still airing keeps your place instead of jumping to the specials or back to the first episode.
• Episode cards show the air date and running time right under the episode's name, and adding an AIOStreams server sets up your Library straight away.

• The posters in Library's Streaming Services row now come to life. The one you're on shows art from that service's most popular titles you can play, drifting slowly and fading to the next title every few seconds; the rest hold a still picture until you move to them.
• With Reduce Motion on, every poster shows a still picture instead.
• With an AIOStreams server added, Library opens faster and stays lighter: Lineup no longer loads every one of your catalogs each time you open the app.

• Fixed live-event syncing appearing stuck at 99%. Previously prepared live events remain ready to play while channels and guide data refresh in the background.
• Improved remote navigation across Sports, TV Guide, Library and Settings, especially with large channel and media libraries.
• The Sports background now fills the entire screen with the highlighted event's dark team-color blend, including behind the navigation bar and scores ticker.
• Live scores refresh independently of channel matching, and tennis events keep their prepared channels when tournament listings change.
• Added soccer coverage for the Carabao Cup, FA Cup, Copa del Rey and Supercopa de España.

• Settings has a new charcoal layout with a fixed category sidebar and more room for controls. The extra description panel and footer text are gone.
• Sports backgrounds follow the highlighted game's dark team-color blend, with smooth transitions as you browse.
• Channel matching shares background work and avoids unnecessary repeat downloads. Saved games remain available while provider data refreshes.
• Reduced rendering work in Sports and Settings, including during rapid remote navigation.

• Saved live events and their matched channels are ready when you reopen Lineup, while schedules and TV listings refresh in the background.
